editorial.headline: Freshwater Aquaculture With A Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 03221 covers the cultivation of non-protected freshwater finfish and other freshwater biota, open across all business scales and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 03221 is the formal home for a broad freshwater aquaculture activity: nursery, rearing, grow-out, breeding, hatchery work, and harvesting of non-protected freshwater finfish and other freshwater biota. The record frames the activity around stock brought to a certain age, form, or size, either for consumption or as input for further grow-out cultivation. In practical terms, it is the controlled raising of freshwater production species rather than ornamental fish or protected aquatic life.

The scope is intentionally rooted in freshwater media. It can take place in inland public freshwater environments such as lakes, reservoirs, rivers, and other bodies of standing water, as well as in artificial facilities that use freshwater as the cultivation medium. The record gives familiar examples: common carp, tilapia, pangasius, gourami, snakehead, toman, mujair, tawes, catfish, and frogs. Those examples help define the commercial character of the code: this is food and production aquaculture, including early-stage breeding or seed production as well as cultivation toward harvest.

On scale, the code is unusually straightforward. It is open to Micro, Small, Medium, and Large businesses, which means the activity can describe a modest local operation as well as a larger structured aquaculture enterprise. For foreign investment, the national position is also clear in the record: the PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no partial cap in the slim record to soften or interpret; nationally, the foreign ownership ceiling is full.

The Bali reading is equally important, because a nationally open activity can still face a local registration barrier. Here, the record does not show a Bali block. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is that OSS risk at Large scale is Medium-High or High, so it is not blocked by the Bali moratorium. The moratorium rule itself remains strict: Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. But for this code, the record’s conclusion is not a red light. A foreign-owned setup is not blocked in Bali on the supplied facts, while still sitting inside a province where the risk classification matters sharply for PMA registration.
